subject: humanities
passage: The Stoic philosopher Epictetus, who had been born into slavery, taught that people suffer less from events themselves than from their judgments about those events. Wealth, reputation, and even health, he argued, lie ultimately beyond our control, whereas our opinions, intentions, and responses are entirely our own. Some readers have taken this teaching as a counsel of passivity. Yet Epictetus did not urge his students to withdraw from the world; he urged them to act well while remaining ______ outcomes they could not command.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: Epictetus taught that outcomes "lie ultimately beyond our control" and that suffering comes from our judgments about events. He asked students to keep acting while accepting results calmly. The blank must mean having come to peaceful acceptance of something: "reconciled to."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Being antagonistic to outcomes would mean opposing or resenting them, which is the kind of disturbing judgment Epictetus warned against.
explanation.B: Correct. To be reconciled to something is to accept it calmly. Epictetus wanted students to act well while accepting outcomes beyond their control.
explanation.C: Incorrect. To be beholden to something is to depend on it. Epictetus taught the opposite: our well-being should not depend on things outside our control.
explanation.D: Incorrect. To be oblivious is to be unaware. Epictetus asked students to accept outcomes, not to fail to notice them.
